components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:40px; padding:0 16px; border:1px solid var(--primary, #203f2d); border-radius:4px; background:var(--primary, #203f2d); color:var(--primary-foreground, #fff8e8); font:700 14px/20px Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition:background-color 100ms ease, border-color 100ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #203f2d) 25%, transparent); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 84%, black); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A visible supporting action on a warm working surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:40px; padding:0 16px; border:1px solid var(--border, #b69d75); border-radius:4px; background:var(--surface-elevated, #f6ead4); color:var(--foreground, #15110d); font:700 14px/20px Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition:background-color 100ms ease, border-color 100ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color:var(--primary, #203f2d); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 8%, var(--surface-elevated, #f6ead4)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline:2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #203f2d) 25%, transparent); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-outline:active { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 12%, var(--surface-elevated, #f6ead4)); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A warm, supporting action with more presence than a ghost control.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:40px; padding:0 16px; border:1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border, #b69d75) 86%, transparent); border-radius:4px; background:var(--secondary, #ead2ad); color:var(--secondary-foreground, #15110d); font:700 14px/20px Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition:border-color 100ms ease, filter 100ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color:var(--border, #b69d75); filter:saturate(1.04); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #203f2d) 25%, transparent); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { filter:brightness(.96); }

components.name: Text Field
components.css: .ds-field { display:grid; gap:8px; color:var(--foreground, #15110d); font-family:Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font-size:12px; line-height:16px; font-weight:600; } .ds-input { box-sizing:border-box; width:100%; height:36px; padding:6px 12px; border:1px solid var(--border, #b69d75); border-radius:4px; background:var(--surface-elevated, #f6ead4); color:var(--foreground, #15110d); font:500 14px/20px Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition:border-color 100ms ease, outline-color 100ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground, #5b5145) 80%, transparent); } .ds-input:hover { border-color:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 30%, var(--border, #b69d75)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color:var(--ring, #203f2d); outline:2px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #203f2d) 25%, transparent); outline-offset:1px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: A compact semantic status label; variants swap the semantic token, not the geometry.
components.css: .ds-badge-success { display:inline-flex; min-height:24px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:2px 10px; border:1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 30%, transparent); border-radius:4px; background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 10%, transparent); color:var(--primary, #203f2d); font:600 12px/16px Manrope, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; white-space:nowrap; transition:background-color 100ms ease; } .ds-badge-success:hover { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #203f2d) 15%, transparent); } .ds-badge-success:focus-visible { outline:3px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #203f2d) 30%, transparent); outline-offset:1px; }

components.name: Section Card

narrative.overview:
The system should feel like the friendly place in a small yard where the useful details live and the community stays in touch. It combines the approachable social character of a tack-room noticeboard with the order of a yard ledger and the practical confidence of a warm field office. Routine operational data is presented with enough visual character to invite attention, never at the expense of reading speed or clarity.

The interface is tactile, friendly, and workmanlike. Warm paper layers, clear rails, compact controls, condensed display headings, and contextual photography keep dense records from feeling dry. It remains contemporary and horse-world adjacent without drifting into rustic decoration, antique styling, or enterprise-dashboard sterility.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, mode-aware paper and earth colors rather than clinical white and grey.
Dense information organized through strong type roles, borders, and tonal layers.
Friendly community character grounded by practical, accountable workflows.
Flat surfaces at rest, with depth created by contrast and structure rather than shadows.
Sparse photography and semantic accent rails used only when they add context or meaning.

rules.name: The Warm Paper Rule
rules.body: Build hierarchy with Oat Canvas, Field Surface, Ledger Paper, Pressed Oat, and Raised Paper; plain white and generic cool grey are not default surfaces.

rules.name: The Working Green Rule
rules.body: Stable Green signals action, selection, focus, or a deliberately branded region; it is not a filler color for arbitrary containers.

rules.name: The Semantic Rail Rule
rules.body: Use four-pixel left rails on repeated records to communicate primary, warning, danger, or muted meaning without flooding the whole card with color.

rules.name: The Noticeboard Headline Rule
rules.body: Use condensed black uppercase type for display hierarchy, not for paragraphs, form labels, or ordinary record titles.

rules.name: The Natural Copy Rule
rules.body: Product copy and data remain in natural case with neutral letter spacing; uppercase is a compact label or display treatment, never a substitute for hierarchy.

rules.name: The Shared Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Start with `16px`, `24px`, or `32px` gaps and `16px`, `20px`, or `24px` padding; introduce a new measurement only when the component has a real geometric constraint.

rules.name: The Work Before Ornament Rule
rules.body: Preserve scannable record order, labels, actions, and responsive collapse before adding editorial asymmetry or imagery.

rules.name: The Flat-But-Layered Rule
rules.body: Separate planes with color, borders, and structure; do not add a shadow to make a component feel finished.

rules.name: The Overlay Exception Rule
rules.body: Transient surfaces may use backdrop blur, z-order, and `100ms`–`350ms` fade/scale motion, but they keep the same bordered paper construction.

rules.name: The Small-Corner Rule
rules.body: Default to `4px` controls, `6px` rows, and `10px` panels; large soft cards and excessive pill geometry do not belong to the incumbent system.

dos: Do use the shared semantic tokens and primitives so light and dark modes preserve the same hierarchy.
Do make routine events and records attractive through display hierarchy, warm surfaces, concise metadata, and meaningful semantic rails.
Do preserve dense, scannable information structure and responsive collapse before adding expression.
Do use contextual horse and yard photography sparingly where it helps users understand place, animal, or workflow.
Do keep interactions legible with visible hover, focus, selected, disabled, error, loading, and reduced-motion states.
donts: Don't replace the warm paper system with plain white cards, cool-grey SaaS chrome, gradients used as decoration, or arbitrary new hues.
Don't add ambient card shadows, glassmorphism, oversized soft corners, or pills where a compact control or row belongs.
Don't turn horse-world character into antique styling, decorative tack motifs, or visual clutter that competes with the records.
Don't use condensed uppercase display type for paragraphs, field labels, ordinary record titles, or long navigation strings.
Don't fabricate local button, card, field, badge, tab, filter, or record-row recipes when a canonical primitive already owns the pattern.
